'''Eyal Hulata''' ({{langx|he|איל חולתא}}; born 1976) is an Israeli security official, who formerly served as the head of the [[National Security Council (Israel)|National Security Council]].

== Early life ==
Eyal Hulata was born in 1976 to Professor Gideon Hulata, a researcher at [[Volcani Center]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=גדעון חולתא |trans-title=Gideon Hulata |publisher=Volcani Institute |date=23 May 2016 |url=https://www.agri.gov.il/he/pages/1545.aspx |archive-date=22 March 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180322010939/https://www.agri.gov.il/he/pages/1545.aspx |language=he }}</ref> and Batya, a biology teacher. His father has roots in the [[Netherlands|Dutch]] city of [[Monnickendam]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=עקבות במוניקנדם |trans-title=Traces in Monnickendam |publisher=Meshotetot |date=7 July 2019 |url=https://meshotetot.wordpress.com/2019/07/07/%D7%A2%D7%A7%D7%91%D7%95%D7%AA-%D7%91%D7%9E%D7%95%D7%A0%D7%99%D7%A7%D7%A0%D7%93%D7%9D/ |archive-date=13 July 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210713094038/https://meshotetot.wordpress.com/2019/07/07/%D7%A2%D7%A7%D7%91%D7%95%D7%AA-%D7%91%D7%9E%D7%95%D7%A0%D7%99%D7%A7%D7%A0%D7%93%D7%9D/ |language=he }}</ref> while his mother immigrated from [[Iranian Jews|Iran]]. Hulata grew up in the city of [[Rishon LeZion]], where he attended [[Gymnasia Realit]] and participated in [[Maccabi Hatzair]].{{citation needed|date= June 2025}}

== Education ==
Hulata received a [[bachelor's degree]] in mathematics and physics from the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]] as part of the [[Talpiot program]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Melman |first=Yossi |date=14 July 2021 |title=Bennett Thinks Outside the Box, Surprises Everybody With New National Security Chief |url=https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/2021-07-14/ty-article/.highlight/bennett-thinks-out-of-the-box-surprises-everybody-with-new-national-security-chief/0000017f-db45-df62-a9ff-dfd77f7f0000 |work=[[Haaretz]]}}</ref>

In 2011, Hulata received a [[PhD]] in [[physics]] from [[Tel Aviv University]], where he wrote a doctoral research on [[Neural network (machine learning)|neural network]] supervised by Professor [[Eshel Ben-Jacob]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=טקס הענקת תואר דוקטור לפילוסופיה |trans-title=Doctor of Philosophy Degree Award Ceremony |publisher=[[Tel Aviv University]] |date=15 June 2011 |url=https://www.tau.ac.il/acad-sec/tekes11/hov.pdf |archive-date=5 July 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110705080755/https://www.tau.ac.il/acad-sec/tekes11/hov.pdf |language=he }}</ref>

Hulata received a [[master's degree]] in [[public administration]] from [[Harvard University]] as part of a program from [[Wexner Foundation]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=הבוגרים שלנו |trans-title=Our Graduates |publisher=[[Wexner Foundation]] |url=https://il.wexnerfoundation.org/our-alumni/ |archive-date=22 September 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200922095431/https://il.wexnerfoundation.org/our-alumni/ |language=he }}</ref>

Hulata has several [[patent]]s filed under his name.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Patents by Inventor Eyal Hulata |publisher=[[Justia]] |url=https://patents.justia.com/inventor/eyal-hulata |archive-date=11 July 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210711160513/https://patents.justia.com/inventor/eyal-hulata }}</ref>

== Public career ==
=== Work in Mossad ===
After his military service, Hulata continued to work in [[Mossad]] for another 17 years in several positions, including the head of technological [[research and development]] and later as head of the team on [[weapons of mass destruction|unconventional weapons]]. Hulata received an [[Israel Defense Prize]] for his work in Mossad.{{citation needed|date= June 2025}}

During this time, there were reports that Hulata did not agree with [[Prime Minister of Israel|Prime Minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] in opposing the [[Iran nuclear deal]], and that he preferred influencing the terms of the agreement rather than oppose it entirely.<ref>{{Cite web |title=איל חולתא, שיתמנה לראש המל"ל, סבר ב-2015 שלא נכון להתנגד להסכם הגרעין |trans-title=Eyal Hulta, who will be appointed head of the National Security Council, believed in 2015 that the nuclear agreement should not be opposed |publisher=[[Times of Israel|Zman Israel]] |date=13 July 2021 |url=https://www.zman.co.il/live/237248/ |archive-date=13 July 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210713131752/https://www.zman.co.il/live/237248/ |language=he }}</ref>

After leaving Mossad, Hulata worked at the [[financial technology]] company {{ill|Pagaya|he|פאגאיה טכנולוגיות}}, where he worked as [[chief process officer]] and was involved in technological entrepreneurship addressing the [[climate crisis]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=MMP סדנה לבכירים: מחקר, פיתוח וניהול מגה-פרויקטים |trans-title=MMP Workshop for Senior Executives: Research, Development and Management of Megaprojects |publisher=[[Technion – Israel Institute of Technology]] |url=https://cont-edu.technion.ac.il/programs/%D7%A0%D7%99%D7%94%D7%95%D7%9C-%D7%99%D7%96%D7%9E%D7%95%D7%AA-%D7%95%D7%A9%D7%99%D7%95%D7%95%D7%A7/mmp-%D7%A1%D7%93%D7%A0%D7%94-%D7%9C%D7%91%D7%9B%D7%99%D7%A8%D7%99%D7%9D-%D7%9E%D7%97%D7%A7%D7%A8-%D7%A4%D7%99%D7%AA%D7%95%D7%97-%D7%95%D7%A0%D7%99%D7%94%D7%95%D7%9C-%D7%9E%D7%92%D7%94-%D7%A4%D7%A8/ |archive-date=15 July 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210715003932/https://cont-edu.technion.ac.il/programs/%D7%A0%D7%99%D7%94%D7%95%D7%9C-%D7%99%D7%96%D7%9E%D7%95%D7%AA-%D7%95%D7%A9%D7%99%D7%95%D7%95%D7%A7/mmp-%D7%A1%D7%93%D7%A0%D7%94-%D7%9C%D7%91%D7%9B%D7%99%D7%A8%D7%99%D7%9D-%D7%9E%D7%97%D7%A7%D7%A8-%D7%A4%D7%99%D7%AA%D7%95%D7%97-%D7%95%D7%A0%D7%99%D7%94%D7%95%D7%9C-%D7%9E%D7%92%D7%94-%D7%A4%D7%A8/ |language=he }}</ref>

=== National Security Advisor ===
[[File:Deputy Secretary Sherman Meets With Israeli National Security Advisor Dr. Hulata (51356618885).jpg|thumb|Israeli National Security advisor Eyal Hulata met with [[United States Deputy Secretary of State|U.S. Deputy State Secretary]] [[Wendy Sherman]] in August 2021 in Washington D.C.]]

Following the establishment of the [[Thirty-sixth government of Israel|36th government]], new [[Prime Minister of Israel|Prime Minister]] [[Naftali Bennett]] appointed Hulata as the new  [[National Security Council (Israel)|National Security Advisor]], replacing the outgoing [[Meir Ben-Shabbat]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bennett taps former senior Mossad official as his new national security adviser |publisher=[[Times of Israel]] |date=11 July 2021 |url=https://www.timesofisrael.com/bennett-taps-former-senior-mossad-official-as-his-new-national-security-adviser/ |archive-date=12 July 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210712093514/https://www.timesofisrael.com/bennett-taps-former-senior-mossad-official-as-his-new-national-security-adviser/ }}</ref> He was approved by the [[Knesset]] a week later, and took office on 15 August 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cabinet approves Mossad's Dr. Eyal Hulata as national security advisor |publisher=[[Jerusalem Post]] |date=19 July 2021 |url=https://www.jpost.com/breaking-news/cabinet-approves-mossads-dr-etal-hulata-as-national-security-advisor-674302 |archive-date=19 July 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210719083814/https://www.jpost.com/breaking-news/cabinet-approves-mossads-dr-etal-hulata-as-national-security-advisor-674302 }}</ref>

In October 2022, following a negotiated settlement of the [[Israeli–Lebanese maritime border dispute]], Hulata stressed that the most important part of the agreement is that Lebanon agreed to end its maritime claims.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ראש המל"ל: "לבנון לא קיבלה מאה אחוז ממה שרצתה" |trans-title=National Security Council Head: "Lebanon Did Not Get 100% of What It Wanted" |publisher=[[Makor Rishon]] |date=12 October 2022 |url=https://www.makorrishon.co.il/news/531883/ |archive-date=12 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221012180535/https://www.makorrishon.co.il/news/531883/ |language=he }}</ref>

Following the formation of the [[Thirty-seventh government of Israel|37th government]], Hulata was replaced by [[Tzachi Hanegbi]] on 8 January 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=היועץ לביטחון לאומי וראש המל"ל איל חולתא סיים את תפקידו |trans-title=National Security Advisor and Head of the National Security Council Eyal Hulta has completed his duties |publisher=[[Government of Israel]] |date=10 January 2023 |url=https://www.gov.il/he/pages/spoke-eyal-hulata100123 |archive-date=18 June 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250618220929/https://www.gov.il/he/pages/spoke-eyal-hulata100123 |language=he }}</ref>

In February 2023, Hulata reflected on Israel's role in [[Peace negotiations in the Russian invasion of Ukraine|peace negotiations]] during the [[Russian invasion of Ukraine]] that he personally helped conduct. He affirmed that he did not regret in the mediation efforts, that "it’s true, we failed, but I was proud we tried".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Inside Israel's failed Ukraine-Russia mediation efforts |publisher=[[Axios (website)|Axios]] |date=22 February 2023 |url=https://www.axios.com/2023/02/22/israel-russia-invasion-ukraine-bennett-mediation-failure |archive-date=22 February 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230222200651/https://www.axios.com/2023/02/22/israel-russia-invasion-ukraine-bennett-mediation-failure }}</ref>

In March 2023, Hulata was appointed as chairman of the [[board of directors]] in the hi-tech company {{ill|Hellman-Aldubi|he|הלמן-אלדובי}}.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ד"ר איל חולתא, לשעבר ראש המל"ל, מצטרף להיי-טק |trans-title=Dr. Eyal Hulta, former head of the National Security Council, joins Hi-Tech |publisher=pc.co.il |date=6 March 2023 |url=https://www.pc.co.il/featured/382451/ |archive-date=6 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230306143658/https://www.pc.co.il/featured/382451/ |language=he }}</ref>

In November 2023, following the [[October 7 attack]], Hulata expressed surprise at [[Hamas]]'s degree of preparation and the [[IDF]]'s lack of defensive mechanisms.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ראש המל"ל לשעבר: ישראל לא תשלוט בעזה, הרש"פ לא מסוגלת לכך |trans-title=Former National Security Council chief: Israel will not control Gaza, the PA is incapable of doing so |publisher=[[Arutz Sheva]] |date=2 November 2023 |url=https://www.inn.co.il/news/618836 |archive-date=2 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231102161924/https://www.inn.co.il/news/618836 |language=he }}</ref>

In May 2025, Hulata criticized the government for lacking a "clear security doctrine" amidst the continuing [[Gaza war]]. He also stressed that "defeating Hamas will not solve the issue of extremism in Gaza", and that it is important to consider important opportunities to reach [[Arab-Israeli normalization|normalization]], citing the success of the [[Abraham Accords]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Israel not prioritizing Iran, beating Hamas won't end Gaza extremism, former security advisor says |publisher=[[Jerusalem Post]] |date=27 May 2025 |url=https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/article-855649 |archive-date=27 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250527152917/https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/article-855649 }}</ref>
